---
title: "The Shape of the Troubles: Visualising and Quantifying Conflict-Attributable Excess Deaths in Young Adult Males in Northern Ireland"
author:
  - name: Jonathan Minton
    orcid: 0000-0003-1207-6259
    email: nate.minton@gmail.com
    corresponding: true
date: last-modified
abstract: |
  This paper argues that an understanding of the human cost of the Troubles in
  Northern Ireland is vital for contemporary policy. This human cost is manifest
  in all-cause mortality records, which are explored visually using Lexis surface
  plots. A model is developed which formalises a key intuition from the data: excess
  deaths in young adult males are represented by a component with peak intensity in
  1972, which then gradually decays over many decades. We call this an
  initiation-decay model, and based on it estimate the Troubles to have cost nearly
  3,000 lives in males aged 15--45 alone, with an intensity half-life of nearly
  seven years. We argue that the conditions which led to this earlier wave of death
  and instability may still be latent in Northern Irish society.
keywords:
  - Northern Ireland
  - Mortality
  - Troubles
  - Data Visualisation
  - Lexis surface
  - Conflict demography
---
